headline: Autonomous AI agents found and exploited zero-days in Redis and NodeBB within hours, and Google answered with CodeMender, an agent that writes patches for the flaws it finds.

emerging_trends.text: Autonomous coding agents such as Kimi K3 now surface exploitable zero-days and write working RCE chains in hours, pushing Redis to ship seven emergency releases and driving Google to answer with its own patch-writing agent.
emerging_trends.topic_title: AI Agents Uncover Redis and NodeBB Zero-Days

emerging_trends.text: Russia-aligned operators keep smuggling malware inside tools people already trust, and UAC-0099 now dresses its MATCHBOIL.V2 loader as a Notepad++ plugin to persist on Ukrainian Windows machines.
emerging_trends.topic_title: UAC-0099 Hides MATCHBOIL.V2 in a Fake Notepad++ Plugin

emerging_trends.text: Data-theft extortion widened its reach as Clop mined Internet-exposed PTC Windchill and FlexPLM servers while a lone hacker threatened to dump two million Origin Energy customer records.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Clop Extorts PTC Windchill and FlexPLM Users

topics.title: AI Agents Uncover Redis and NodeBB Zero-Days
topics.latest_developments: Redis shipped seven security releases on July 23 after researchers drove Moonshot's Kimi K3 agents to find memory-corruption flaws and publish authenticated RCE proof-of-concepts against stock Redis 6.2.22, 7.4.9, 8.6.4, and 8.8.0, while Aikido Security's AI pentest agents found eight high-severity flaws in NodeBB during a six-hour source review and Google previewed CodeMender, an agent that confirms exploitability and writes fixes.
topics.summary: AI systems now discover and weaponize software flaws at machine speed, forcing vendors like Redis and NodeBB to patch and prompting defenders such as Google to automate remediation; administrators should move to Redis 6.2.23, 7.2.15, or 7.4.10 and NodeBB 4.14.2.

sources.title: Kimi K3 Agents Found Redis Zero-Days and Built RCE Exploit, Researchers Say
NodeBB Patches Eight AI-Found Flaws Exposing Admin Access and Private Chats
Google gives developers an AI bug hunter that also writes patches
Is Patching Dead? Vulnerability Management in the Post-Mythos Era

topics.title: Origin Energy Breach Exposes Australian Customers
topics.latest_developments: Origin Energy confirmed that an unauthorized party accessed and leaked customer data online, as a hacker claimed to hold the personal information of 2 million Origin customers and threatened to publish it.
topics.summary: Origin Energy, one of Australia's largest energy suppliers, disclosed a breach exposing customer personally identifiable information and is still counting how many Australians the theft touched; affected customers should watch for fraud and phishing.

sources.title: Data Breach Confirmed After Australian Energy Giant Origin Is Hacked
Australian energy provider Origin says data breach exposes client data
Major Australian energy supplier confirms customer data compromised

topics.title: UAC-0099 Hides MATCHBOIL.V2 in a Fake Notepad++ Plugin
topics.latest_developments: Ukraine's CERT-UA warned that the Russia-aligned cluster UAC-0099 now ships an archive bundling the legitimate Notepad++ application with a malicious utility called LunchPoke, disguised as a plugin, to establish persistence and deliver the MATCHBOIL.V2 payload on Windows systems.
topics.summary: UAC-0099, a Russia-aligned group that previously weaponized WinRAR flaws against Ukrainian targets, hides its malware inside a trusted editor's plugin directory; defenders should scrutinize unexpected Notepad++ archives and plugin utilities.

sources.title: Fake Notepad++ Plugin Delivers MATCHBOIL.V2 in UAC-0099 Attacks
Hackers abuse Notepad++ plugins to stealthily install malware

topics.title: Clop Extorts PTC Windchill and FlexPLM Users
topics.latest_developments: BleepingComputer reported the Clop ransomware gang, also tracked as Cl0p, is hunting Internet-exposed PTC Windchill and FlexPLM product-lifecycle-management instances in a new data-theft extortion campaign.
topics.summary: Clop, the crew known for mass-exploiting managed file-transfer and enterprise software, now steals data from exposed PTC Windchill and FlexPLM servers and threatens to leak it; organizations running those systems should restrict Internet exposure and hunt for intrusion.

sources.title: Clop ransomware targets Windchill, FlexPLM in data theft attacks

topics.title: Laundry Bear Zimbra Espionage Reveals Full Mailbox Theft
topics.latest_developments: BleepingComputer tied the Russian state-sponsored group Laundry Bear to the alias Void Blizzard, and The Hacker News detailed the Zimbra webmail payload harvesting each victim's last 90 days of email, the full organizational directory, the browser-saved password, and the two-factor recovery codes, with Unit 42 mapping the JavaScript injection behind the credential theft.
topics.summary: Laundry Bear, a Kremlin-backed espionage group, has read Western government and commercial mailboxes since July 2025 through a zero-click Zimbra Collaboration Suite flaw that a victim triggers merely by previewing a message; the NSA, CISA, and partner agencies urge patching in advisory AA26-204A.

sources.title: Russian State-Supported Cyber Actors Conduct Phishing Campaign Targeting Users of Zimbra Collaboration Suite
Russian Espionage Group Exploited Zimbra Zero-Day to Steal Mail and 2FA Codes
Russian Global Webmail Espionage
Russian hackers exploit Zimbra zero-click flaw for email theft

topics.title: RefluXFS Grants Root Through Linux XFS Race Condition
topics.latest_developments: BleepingComputer detailed RefluXFS, tracked as CVE-2026-64600, a nine-year-old race condition in the Linux kernel's XFS filesystem that lets a local attacker overwrite protected files and escalate to root.
topics.summary: The long-dormant XFS flaw affects Linux systems using the widely deployed filesystem and hands local users full root control; administrators should apply kernel updates as distributions ship fixes.

sources.title: New RefluXFS Linux flaw lets attackers gain root privileges

business_politics.title: Oil Tops $100, Driving a Global Bond Selloff
business_politics.latest_developments: Brent crude settled above $100 a barrel Thursday, heading for a weekly gain of more than 12% and pushing Treasury yields to the highest levels of President Trump's second term.
business_politics.summary: Red Sea attacks by Yemen's Houthis on oil shipping have spurred a surge in Brent crude that lifted the 2-year and 10-year Treasury yields, dragged equities lower, and stoked bets the Federal Reserve will raise rates—a squeeze that tightens financial conditions worldwide and threatens Republican midterm hopes.

business_politics.title: Houthis Hit Saudi Tankers; Trump Threatens Iran
business_politics.latest_developments: The Houthis fired on two Saudi oil tankers in the Red Sea, and Trump vowed 'major military punishment,' saying he will hold Iran responsible for future Houthi attacks.
business_politics.summary: Yemen's Houthi militants have opened a new front in the U.S.-Iran war by threatening Red Sea oil shipments through one of the world's most vital waterways, and with the conflict in its fifth month Trump has grown skeptical of diplomacy and, per a senior administration official, entered 'revenge mode' against Tehran.

sources.title: Trump Says Iran Will Be Held Responsible for Future Houthi Attacks

around_town.title: Pennsylvania Eases School Lead-Reporting Standard
around_town.latest_developments: The state budget quietly relaxed the standard for lead reporting in Pennsylvania schools, and the Post-Gazette reported July 24 that the law's problems run deeper still.
around_town.summary: A provision in the new state budget loosened the threshold at which Pennsylvania schools must report lead in drinking water, a change the Post-Gazette found compounds longstanding weaknesses in the commonwealth's school lead-testing law.

sources.title: Pennsylvania's budget quietly relaxed a standard for lead reporting in schools. Issues with the law go much deeper.

around_town.title: Ambulance Bills Escape Federal Surprise-Billing Ban
around_town.latest_developments: PublicSource reported July 24 that Washington's crackdown on surprise medical bills left out ground ambulances, exposing Southwestern Pennsylvania patients to large out-of-network charges.
around_town.summary: When Congress barred most surprise medical bills, it exempted ground ambulance rides, so a Southwestern Pennsylvania patient can still face a bill topping $400 for an unplanned trip, a gap that hits rural residents hardest.

sources.title: Congress didn’t ban shocking ambulance bills, leaving rural patients especially vulnerable
